section_1.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Digital Puppet'
section_1.content: Introduce linear transformations as a transformation of a 2D coordinate grid. Use the analogy of a rubber sheet being stretched or rotated. Define the prerequisite: vectors as arrows (x, y).
section_1.example: A 2D character avatar on a screen stretching its arms—visualize the grid squares deforming while remaining parallel and equally spaced.

section_2.title: The Basis Vectors: The DNA of Transformation
section_2.content: Explain that any transformation is defined by where the basis vectors (i-hat: [1,0] and j-hat: [0,1]) land. If i-hat moves to [a,c] and j-hat moves to [b,d], the transformation is fully captured.
section_2.example: Animate i-hat (red arrow) moving to (2, 0) and j-hat (green arrow) moving to (0, 1.5). Show the grid morphing into a rectangle.

section_3.title: The Matrix as a Transformation Recipe
section_3.content: Formalize the concept: The columns of a 2x2 matrix are the landing spots of our basis vectors. Multiplying a vector by a matrix is simply tracking where that vector's 'components' land in the new space.
section_3.example: Represent the transformation [2, 0; 0, 1.5] acting on a vector [1, 1]. Show the math: 1*[2, 0] + 1*[0, 1.5] = [2, 1.5].

section_4.title: Dynamic Visualization: Rotation and Shear
section_4.content: Demonstrate that different matrices create different spatial effects. Introduce specific matrices for 90-degree rotation vs. 'shearing' (tilting).
section_4.example: Animate a cat icon: Applying a shear matrix [1, 1; 0, 1] causes the cat to tilt sideways as if hit by a breeze, keeping its paws on the floor.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Recap: Linear transformations preserve origin and grid lines. The matrix is just a compact, numerical 'map' of the geometric deformation.
section_5.example: A final 5-second animation overlaying a static 'input' grid with a morphed 'output' grid, showing the matrix equation linking the two.
